clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old female with leukocytosis and mild left upper quadrant discomfort underwent abdominal CT revealing thickening and nodular abnormality at the gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) and liver hypodensities suggestive of metastases. Upper endoscopy identified a fungating mass at the GEJ. Biopsy was performed, and histopathology confirmed adenocarcinoma with HER2 overexpression (3+). Clinical progression included leukocytosis without infection and symptomatic anemia.
